description:
From the fz-kdt.106 cold review (2026-09-01). On a 34-line program (14
element families x 14 distinct lambdas through Enum.all?/2, parked at the
review scratchpad as kdt106-review-stress1.fz) the base compiler at
1d44ac7cd spends 172.8s and emits 526 executables with 24 budget
collapses; with dominance absorption it spends 1.63s and emits 588 with
3. Same stdout, both schedules confluent. Two consequences:

(1) The artifact RISES by 62 executables under the fix -- so "counts must
not rise anywhere" is not a property of the design; the correct gate is a
CLASSIFICATION gate: a rise is acceptable exactly when paired with a
reduction in budget collapses on that fixture (precision replacing
collapse-widened sharing). Recorded here as the standing rationale.

(2) The real signal is compile WORK, and nothing in fixtures2 captures a
100x collapse cascade. Add a corpus fixture in this shape with a
work-based ratchet (settlement counts from --log-telemetry, per
fz-f98.23's no-wall-clock law), not a wall-clock one, once the
fz-kdt.106-landed baseline exists to pin against.
title: Budget-collapse cascades are a compile-work catastrophe the corpus never captures: add a collapse-cascade fixture with a work ratchet
